disease_label_per_paper: Aspiration pneumonia with Sarcina ventriculi bacteremia in an elderly man with COPD after hip arthroplasty

past_history: COPD on home oxygen therapy 2 L/min
right femoral neck fracture treated with bipolar hip arthroplasty

presentation_summary: An 89-year-old man with prior cerebral infarction and COPD on home oxygen was admitted for right femoral neck fracture.
Bipolar hip arthroplasty was performed on hospital day 3.
On day 6 he became febrile and expectorated copious sputum, with temperature 39.6 C, RR 28/min, and SpO2 80% while breathing 2 L/min oxygen by nasal prongs.
Blood tests showed CRP 219.1 mg/L, WBC 7.3 x10^9/L, hemoglobin 86 g/L, platelets 112 x10^9/L, albumin 20 g/L, urea nitrogen 5.7 mmol/L, and creatinine 53 umol/L.
Chest CT showed aspirated sputum in the main bronchus, mild lung infiltration, and old COPD-related lung damage.

confirmatory_findings.finding: Sputum Gram stain with tetrad Gram-positive cocci
confirmatory_findings.source_text_value: large Gram-positive cocci clustered in tetrads were present in sputum
anaerobic blood culture bottle positive at 47 hours; 16S rDNA sequencing confirmed Sarcina ventriculi

confirmatory_findings.finding: No potential infectious source other than respiratory tract identified
confirmatory_findings.source_text_value: no potential infectious source other than the respiratory tract was identified

actual_treatment.name: ceftriaxone 2 g daily for five days
sputum, urine, and blood microbiology testing

outcome_follow_up.description: Fever resolved two days after starting ceftriaxone, respiratory function recovered to pre-admission level, and he was discharged without further complications.

quality_warnings: Sarcina species identification, susceptibility, lack of alternative source, ceftriaxone response, and discharge are confirmatory/non-ranking.
Rankable evidence is limited to the clinical episode, labs, hypoxemia, and CT evidence of aspirated sputum plus lung infiltration.
